chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Indeed, the servant stands up and fulfills the optional prayer, so the Lord is astonished by His angels regarding him, so He says: 'O My angels! My servant is fulfilling what I did not obligate upon him.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of performing voluntary prayers according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) illustrates the profound spiritual elevation achieved through voluntary prayers (nafilah), noting that Allah delights the angels by highlighting the servant's initiative in fulfilling what was not strictly mandated. This emphasizes the Shia scholarly view that nafilah serves as a means of drawing closer to God (taqarrub) and perfecting the obligatory duties, reflecting the divine pleasure (ridwan) for extra devotion.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Abu Najran, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘If the servant stand to fulfil (outstanding) Optional Salāt, so the Lordazwj is Astounded to Hisazwj Angels due to it, so Heazwj is Saying: “O Myazwj Angels! Myazwj servant is fulfilling what Iazwj did not Obligate upon him”’.
en.sarwar: 8. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn abu Najran from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that a servant of Allah may rise to perform Qada’ (compensatory prayer for) an optional Salah (prayer) that was missed in its proper time. The Lord then expresses surprise before the angels saying, ‘My angels, look at My servant who makes up for the optional Salah (prayer) missed in time, when I have not even made it obligatory for him.’”
